column1: # *** RECORDS READ ABOUT A NAMED PERSON, SO THAT THEIR OWN PAGE CAN SAY SO. ***
# Created 17 September 2026 after a fault found in the Mazza archive was looked for here and found in
# a different shape. *** This archive had no slug-keyed evidence file at all: a person page is built
# from lerena-register.tsv and relations.tsv and NOTHING ELSE. *** So a whole session's worth of
# records could be written into topic files, rendered on topic pages, and never reach the person -
# whose page went on saying "No relationships are recorded for this person. The source names them and
# nothing more." *** That is what it was doing for Cipriano and Vitalino of Trinidad while this archive
# held their wives, their children and their parents. ***
# person: MUST match a name in lerena-register.tsv exactly. The build FAILS if it does not - it does
#   not skip the row, which is the mistake relations.tsv makes.
# The build attaches these to the person and the page renders them under "What has been read".

column2: *** HIS PARENTS: MAURICIO LERENA and CASIMIRA MONTANA. *** Death registration of 1928 at Flores, record 40, entry 1, page 20v. *** This makes him a grandson of Ramon Serena of Valdemoro and a first cousin of Bernabe. *** Indexed only - the card says "Image Unavailable", so the act itself has not been read.
Married *** LAURIANA BELOQUI ***; three children baptised at Trinidad, Flores - Doroteo Donato (1875), Maria Leonor (1877) and Lauriana (1891).

column2: Named again as a father on the death entry of *** ROSAURA FULGENCIA LERENA *** at Trinidad - "parents Vitalino Lerena, Andrea Atcheverre". *** The mother's Basque surname is spelled Echeverry, Echeverse, Etcheverre and Atcheverre across four records of one family. ***

*** Named as a father on his son's marriage act: *** "Fausto G. Lerena, born 1880, married 7 April 1900 at *** SANTISIMA TRINIDAD, Trinidad, Flores ***, parents *** BERNABE LERENA and CASIMIRA PELAEZ. ***"

column1: Dona Casimira PELAEZ (wife of Bernabe LERENA)
column2: Named as the mother on the same 1900 marriage act of her son Fausto G. Lerena at Trinidad. *** The Lerenas and Pelaezes of Trinidad intermarried until the church required a dispensation for consanguinity in 1885. ***

*** HIS SON'S BAPTISM NAMES HIS OWN PARENTS. *** Luis Escolastico, baptised Iglesia Matriz, Montevideo, 10 February 1811 - "abuelos paternos *** FELIZ GERENA y ROSALIA AGUILAR ***". *** And the 1812 act of a DIFFERENT family, one year later at the same font, writes ITS grandfather "SALVADOR GERENA" *** - the same clerk-world spelling, which is why the two houses had to be told apart by where they came from rather than by how they were written.

*** His son ALBERTO's death is now on a record, not a tree. *** Montevideo civil registration, *** certificate 246 ***, death 1 March 1921: "Alberto Lerena, 69, born about 1852, father *** AVELINO LERENA ***, mother *** AMBROSIA TREIBEL ***, wife Maria Ines Larriera." *** The archive held the Lerena Traibel children on FamilySearch tree IDs; this is the first of them with a register behind it. ***

Her marriage act, re-read from the index 17 September 2026: *** "Justa Pastora Llerena, natural de CANELONES, residente en el CORDON, soltera - 3 November 1830, Iglesia San Pablo, Cordon, Montevideo, certificate 3 - hija de SANCHO LLERENA y MARIA FERNANDEZ" ***, marrying *** MANUEL BARROS, natural de PERNAMBUCO ***. *** Already held from the 1831 Cordon act; recorded here because a record about a person belongs on her page. ***

*** HER BIRTH REGISTRATION, FOUND. *** Births, December quarter 1884, *** BIDEFORD, volume 5b page 506 *** - a birth on 17 September registered within the six weeks the law allowed falls in the December quarter. *** The woman who married Pablo Armando at St Dominic's, Wynberg, on 3 September 1911 now has her own birth on an index. ***

*** Her nine brothers and sisters were all found in the same index and then followed to their deaths *** - and four married surnames came out of it: Isabella Temple married *** HENRY DALLING ***, Lucy Elizabeth married *** WILLIAM NORRISH SWEET ***, Irene married *** HENRY ALBERT BURTON ***, Agnes Walker married *** ALFRED S WOOD ***. *** Mary Septima is the only one of the ten who is not in the English death index: she died at Cape Town in 1935. She is the one who left. ***
column3: England & Wales, GRO Marriage and Death Indexes (FreeBMD)

column2: *** Named as the mother of a child baptised into slavery in Sancho Lerena's household: *** "En veinte y seis de Septiembre de mil ochocientos doce: Yo el infrascrito bautice solemnemente a MARIA MERCEDES, que nacio antes de ayer, NEGRA ESCLAVA DE DON SANCHO LERENA Y DE DONA MARIA FERNANDEZ, hija de JUANA. Madrina Catalina Martinez." *** The 1812 padron counted four enslaved people in that household at calle San Juan No 60 and named none of them. This act names her. ***
column3: Montevideo, Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, baptism act, 26 September 1812

column2: *** Born 24 September 1812 and baptised two days later, in slavery, in the household of Sancho Lerena and Maria Fernandez. *** "En veinte y seis de Septiembre de mil ochocientos doce: Yo el infrascrito bautice solemnemente a MARIA MERCEDES, que nacio antes de ayer, NEGRA ESCLAVA DE DON SANCHO LERENA Y DE DONA MARIA FERNANDEZ, hija de JUANA. Madrina Catalina Martinez." *** Her godmother was Catalina Martinez. *** Nothing further about her is known - not a marriage, not a death, not an emancipation.
column3: Montevideo, Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, baptism act, 26 September 1812

column2: *** HIS PARENTS, OFF THE PAGE RATHER THAN OFF A TREE. *** "el matrimonio que por palabras de presente contrajo Don GILBERTO LERENA, Oriental, soltero, hijo legitimo de Don LUIS y de Dona JUSTINIANA LENGUAS: con [Julia] SALVANACH, del propio estado y nacionalidad, e hija de Don CRISTOBAL y de Dona ANGELA ALVAREZ" - padrinos "Don LUIS LERENA y Dona ANGELA ALVAREZ". He is *** 'Oriental, soltero' *** - Uruguayan and a bachelor - and the third banns were dispensed by *** Don Jacinto Vera, Vicario Apostolico. *** *** THE MACHINE INDEX OF THIS SAME ACT IS WRONG ABOUT THE BRIDE: *** it gives her a father called 'Cristobal LERENA'. The page shows *** Cristobal is a SALVANACH, her own father ***, and the surname Lerena was carried across from the padrino line. *** There is no Cristobal Lerena. ***
column3: Montevideo, San Francisco de Asis, religious marriage no. 178, 11 August 1877, image read

column2: *** CORROBORATED BY A SECOND DOCUMENT OF THE SAME YEAR. *** The 1812 padron of Montevideo enters her inside Sancho Lerena's household at *** calle San Juan No 60 ***, among four enslaved people named *** ANTONIO, JOSE, JUANA and TERESA *** - listed after the six children and before *** RODRIGO FERNANDEZ ***, the father-in-law, who closes the household. *** Until now she was known only from the baptism act of 26 September 1812, which calls her the mother of Maria Mercedes. *** Two independent records, the same household, the same year. *** A DIFFERENT JUANA, aged 41, heads house 59 on the same page and is not her. ***
